name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
    # Optional: Only run on specific file changes
    # paths:
    #   - "src/**/*.ts"
    #   - "src/**/*.tsx"
    #   - "src/**/*.js"
    #   - "src/**/*.jsx"

jobs:
  claude-review:
    # Optional: Filter by PR author
    # if: |
    #   github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'external-contributor' ||
    #   github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'new-developer' ||
    #   github.event.pull_request.author_association == 'FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR'

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Run Claude Code Review
        id: claude-review
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          prompt: |
            REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
            PR NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}

            Please review this pull request and provide feedback on:
            - Code quality and best practices
            - Potential bugs or issues
            - Performance considerations
            - Security concerns
            - Test coverage

            Use the repository's CLAUDE.md for guidance on style and conventions. Be constructive and helpful in your feedback.

            Use `gh pr comment` with your Bash tool to leave your review as a comment on the PR.

          # See https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/usage.md
          # or https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/cli-reference for available options
          claude_args: '--allowed-tools "Bash(gh issue view:*),Bash(gh search:*),Bash(gh issue list:*),Bash(gh pr comment:*),Bash(gh pr diff:*),Bash(gh pr view:*),Bash(gh pr list:*)"'

name: Claude Code

on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    types: [opened, assigned]
  pull_request_review:
    types: [submitted]

jobs:
  claude:
    if: |
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review_comment' && contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_review' && contains(github.event.review.body, '@claude')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' && (contains(github.event.issue.body, '@claude') || contains(github.event.issue.title, '@claude')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
      id-token: write
      actions: read # Required for Claude to read CI results on PRs
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Run Claude Code
        id: claude
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}

          # This is an optional setting that allows Claude to read CI results on PRs
          additional_permissions: |
            actions: read

          # Optional: Give a custom prompt to Claude. If this is not specified, Claude will perform the instructions specified in the comment that tagged it.
          # prompt: 'Update the pull request description to include a summary of changes.'

          # Optional: Add claude_args to customize behavior and configuration
          # See https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/usage.md
          # or https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/cli-reference for available options
          # claude_args: '--allowed-tools Bash(gh pr:*)'

# .github/workflows/iso-4217.yml

name: Refresh the ISO 4217 currency list
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

# one run at a time, so a manual dispatch and the schedule cannot push the branch out of order
concurrency:
  group: iso-4217
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  refresh:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf 'latest\n' > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: "latest"
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - id: list
        run: nub run update:iso4217
      # nothing to do when main already carries the list, or when the open generated PR does: only the list is compared, so an unrelated edit to the file on main does not replace a reviewed head
      - id: diff
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CODES: ${{ steps.list.outputs.codes }}
        run: |
          changed=true
          if git diff --quiet -- packages/zod/src/v4/core/regexes.ts; then
            changed=false
          elif [ -n "$(gh pr list --head iso-4217 --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')" ] && git fetch -q origin iso-4217; then
            head_codes=$(git show FETCH_HEAD:packages/zod/src/v4/core/regexes.ts | node -e 'process.stdout.write(require("fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8").match(/currencyCode: RegExp =\s+\/\^\(\?:([A-Z|]+)\)\$\//)?.[1] ?? "")')
            [ "$head_codes" = "$CODES" ] && changed=false
          fi
          echo "changed=$changed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # a PR opened with the workflow token never triggers the test workflow, so the tests that read the list run here
      - if: steps.diff.outputs.changed == 'true'
        run: nub exec --node vitest run packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/string.test.ts packages/zod/src/v4/mini/tests/string.test.ts packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/to-json-schema.test.ts
      - if: steps.diff.outputs.changed == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HUSKY: "0"
          PUBLISHED: ${{ steps.list.outputs.published }}
          ADDED: ${{ steps.list.outputs.added }}
          REMOVED: ${{ steps.list.outputs.removed }}
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git checkout -B iso-4217
          git add packages/zod/src/v4/core/regexes.ts
          git commit -m "fix: refresh the ISO 4217 currency list ($PUBLISHED)"
          git push --force origin iso-4217
          title="Refresh the ISO 4217 currency list ($PUBLISHED)"
          printf 'The ISO 4217 list published %s changed the active currency codes.\n\n- added: %s\n- removed: %s\n\nGenerated by `nub run update:iso4217` from the SIX Group list. `z.currencyCode()` accepts the new set once this merges.\n' "$PUBLISHED" "${ADDED:-none}" "${REMOVED:-none}" > /tmp/body.md
          gh pr create --base main --head iso-4217 --title "$title" --body-file /tmp/body.md || gh pr edit iso-4217 --title "$title" --body-file /tmp/body.md

# .github/release.yml

name: Release on npm
on:
  # Dispatch only, and deliberately so. A `workflow_dispatch` needs a GitHub session or token carrying write access; a stolen git push credential carries neither, so it can no longer start a release by landing a commit or cutting a tag. That is the shape of the 2026-09-21 nubjs/nub compromise, where a stolen push credential cut a tag and 18 packages published unattended. A version bump on main is therefore inert: a maintainer runs `gh workflow run release.yml`, approves the npm environment, and then approves each staged version on npm with 2FA.
  #
  # One run, three release jobs. `stage` puts both versions in npm's staged queue. `approval` is a job on the `release-approval` environment, whose required reviewer is the maintainer: GitHub holds the run there, with no runner, for up to 30 days. The npm approval is the gate; the environment approval only resumes the run, and `finish` checks the registry before it tags or releases anything. `stager approve` does both, approving on npm and then resuming the run.
  workflow_dispatch:

# one release at a time, held across the approval wait, so a second dispatch queues instead of staging next to a held run; never cancelled, since a run mid-`npm stage publish` must finish
concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  test-node:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        node: ["lts/*"]
        # Deliberately narrower than test.yml, which also runs a "latest" leg. This
        # matrix gates publishing, so a regression in a bleeding-edge compiler must
        # not be able to block a release. test.yml carries the TypeScript 7 signal.
        typescript: ["5.5", "6"]
    name: Test with TypeScript ${{ matrix.typescript }} on Node ${{ matrix.node }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    steps:
      # A step, not a job-level `if:`: a skipped job is silent, and the run would go green having released nothing while looking like it had. This job gates the publish, so failing here stops the release.
      - name: Refuse to release from any ref but main
        run: |
          [ "$GITHUB_REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] || { echo "::error::release.yml runs from main only, got $GITHUB_REF"; exit 1; }

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf '%s\n' "${{ matrix.node }}" > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      # Build with the repo-pinned TypeScript, which is what actually ships. zshy
      # uses the classic compiler API, which TypeScript 7 no longer provides.
      - run: nub run build
      - run: nub add typescript@${{ matrix.typescript }} -Dw
      - run: nub run test
      - run: nub run --filter @zod/resolution test:all
      - run: nub run --filter @zod/integration test:all

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node: ["latest"]
    name: Lint on Node ${{ matrix.node }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf '%s\n' "${{ matrix.node }}" > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: nub run format:check
      - run: nub run lint:check

  check-circular:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Check for circular dependencies
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf 'latest\n' > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: "latest"
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: nub run check:circular

  stage:
    needs: [test-node, lint, check-circular]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # a required reviewer approves every run, and the environment only deploys main; npm's trusted publishers are bound to it so no other branch or workflow can even stage. The environment is the first of two gates — the second is the 2FA approval of each staged version, which this job cannot perform.
    environment: npm
    # this job only builds and stages; the wait for the approval is the `approval` job, which holds no runner
    timeout-minutes: 60
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    outputs:
      zod: ${{ steps.version.outputs.zod }}
      mini: ${{ steps.version.outputs.mini }}
      # both versions are served already (a re-dispatch after the approval), so there is nothing to wait for and `approval` is skipped
      served: ${{ steps.served.outputs.served }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      
      - name: Set up Nub
        uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          registry-url: https://registry.npmjs.org/

      # `npm stage publish` landed in npm 11.15, later than the npm bundled with any Node the
      # action provisions. setup-nub fronts that Node's bin dir on PATH, so the global install
      # lands in the same prefix the `npm` below resolves from — the echo proves which one.
      - name: Install an npm CLI that can stage
        run: | # zizmor: ignore[adhoc-packages] the npm CLI itself, pinned to the major that carries `npm stage`
          npm install -g npm@11
          v="$(npm --version)"
          # `sort -V | head -1` yields the smaller of the two; it has to be the floor.
          [ "$(printf '%s\n11.15.0\n' "$v" | sort -V | head -1)" = "11.15.0" ] \
            || { echo "::error::npm $v cannot stage (need >= 11.15)"; exit 1; }
          echo "npm $v at $(command -v npm)"

      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: nub run build
      - run: nub run test
      - run: nub run --filter @zod/resolution test:all
      - run: nub run prepublishOnly
        working-directory: ./packages/zod
      - run: nub run prepublishOnly
        working-directory: ./packages/mini

      # read versions even when publishing skips an existing release
      - name: Resolve the versions
        id: version
        run: |
          echo "zod=$(nub --node -p "require('./packages/zod/package.json').version")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "mini=$(nub --node -p "require('./packages/mini/package.json').version")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # This job cannot publish. Both trusted publishers are stage-only, so all it can do is put a version in npm's staged queue, where it is not installable and its number is reserved; a maintainer then approves it with 2FA. A credential that reaches this workflow can therefore fill a queue and nothing else.
      - name: Stage zod on npm
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.zod }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/npm-stage-publish.sh packages/zod --provenance

      # @zod/mini ships in lockstep with zod and is a no-op when its version is already on the registry, so it runs unconditionally (the first release of the scoped package rides on a merge that does not bump zod itself). It is staged here, next to zod and before the wait, so both versions are in the queue when the maintainer sits down: one approval session covers the pair, and `pnpm stage approve` takes them under a single one-time password. Under the old irreversible publish this step ran last, so that a failed @zod/mini publish could not cost zod its tag; staging removes that hazard, because a failure here leaves zod staged and unapproved rather than live and unmatched.
      - name: Stage @zod/mini on npm
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.mini }}
        run: bash .github/scripts/npm-stage-publish.sh packages/mini --provenance --access public

      - name: Check whether npm serves both versions
        id: served
        env:
          ZOD_VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.zod }}
          MINI_VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.mini }}
        run: |
          if curl -sf "https://registry.npmjs.org/zod/$ZOD_VERSION" > /dev/null && curl -sf "https://registry.npmjs.org/@zod%2fmini/$MINI_VERSION" > /dev/null; then
            echo "served=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "zod@$ZOD_VERSION and @zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION are both served; no approval to wait for"
          else
            echo "served=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Say how to approve
        if: steps.served.outputs.served != 'true'
        env:
          ZOD_VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.zod }}
          MINI_VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.mini }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016  # the backticks below are markdown for the step summary, not command substitution
          {
            echo "## Staged on npm, waiting for approval"
            echo
            echo "- \`zod@$ZOD_VERSION\`"
            echo "- \`@zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION\`"
            echo
            echo 'Neither version is installable until a maintainer approves it with 2FA. This run is now held on the `release-approval` environment, with no runner, for up to 30 days. It resumes when that deployment is approved, and `finish` then waits for npm to serve both versions before it tags, releases and publishes to JSR.'
            echo
            echo '```'
            echo "stager approve 'zod@$ZOD_VERSION' '@zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION'   # approve both in the browser, then resume this run"
            echo "stager reject 'zod@$ZOD_VERSION' '@zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION'    # drop both staged versions and fail this run"
            echo '```'
            echo
            echo "Without stager: read the stage ids with \`npm stage list zod\` and \`npm stage list @zod/mini\`, then approve each with \`npm stage approve <id>\`; \`pnpm stage approve\` takes both in one interactive picker under a single one-time password, as does the Staged Packages tab on npmjs.com. Then approve the pending \`release-approval\` deployment on $RUN_URL."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  approval:
    # held by the environment's required reviewer, not by a runner: GitHub keeps the run waiting for up to 30 days, with no six-hour cap, until the deployment is approved. It is a resume signal only; a version nobody approved on npm still stops `finish` at the registry check.
    needs: stage
    if: needs.stage.outputs.served != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release-approval
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - env:
          ZOD_VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.zod }}
          MINI_VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.mini }}
        run: echo "resuming; finish checks that npm serves zod@$ZOD_VERSION and @zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION"

  finish:
    needs: [stage, approval]
    # `approval` is skipped when npm already serves both versions, and `finish` still runs then to create whatever an earlier run did not; the explicit condition drops the implicit `success()`, so `stage` is checked by name
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.stage.result == 'success' && (needs.approval.result == 'success' || (needs.approval.result == 'skipped' && needs.stage.outputs.served == 'true')) }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # 6h is GitHub's hard cap for a hosted runner; the wait takes 340 minutes of it and the steps after it need a few
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      # THE HUMAN GATE. The run resumes on the environment approval, which says nothing about npm, so the tag, the GitHub release and both JSR publishes wait here until the registry serves both versions; nothing public ever describes a version npm did not ship. The loop also absorbs the automated review npm runs once a version is approved, which held 4.5.0 for 16 minutes, 4.5.3 for 25 and 4.6.0 for 116; none of those is an upper bound. If the approval comes later, re-run this job.
      - name: Wait for npm to serve both versions
        env:
          ZOD_VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.zod }}
          MINI_VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.mini }}
        run: |
          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 340 * 60 ))
          wait_for () {
            local label="$1" url="$2" i=0
            until curl -sf "$url" > /dev/null; do
              if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then
                echo "::error::$label is still not served after 340 minutes; if it was never approved on npm, approve it with 2FA (stager approve '$label'), then re-run this job"
                exit 1
              fi
              i=$((i + 1))
              if [ $((i % 15)) -eq 0 ]; then echo "$label is not served yet ($i minutes)"; fi
              sleep 60
            done
            echo "$label is live"
          }
          wait_for "zod@$ZOD_VERSION" "https://registry.npmjs.org/zod/$ZOD_VERSION"
          wait_for "@zod/mini@$MINI_VERSION" "https://registry.npmjs.org/@zod%2fmini/$MINI_VERSION"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Nub
        uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"

      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Configure changelog
        run: |
          printf '%s\n' '{"categories": [], "template": "## Commits:\n\n#{{UNCATEGORIZED}}", "pr_template": "- #{{MERGE_SHA}} #{{TITLE}}"}' > changelog_config.json
          cat changelog_config.json
          echo "last_tag=$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # the run's commit rather than `github.ref`: main may have moved on while the run was held
      - name: Generate changelog
        id: github_release
        uses: mikepenz/release-changelog-builder-action@v6
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          fromTag: "${{ env.last_tag }}"
          toTag: ${{ github.sha }}
          mode: COMMIT
          configuration: changelog_config.json

      # notes go through env and a file so a commit subject can't break out of the command
      - name: Create release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.zod }}
          CHANGELOG: ${{ steps.github_release.outputs.changelog }}
        run: |
          if gh release view "v$VERSION" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "v$VERSION is already released"
            exit 0
          fi
          printf '%s' "$CHANGELOG" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release_notes.md"
          # the job token cannot write a ref once main has moved past this commit with a workflow change, which a run held for days makes likely
          gh release create "v$VERSION" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --target "$GITHUB_SHA" \
            --title "v$VERSION" \
            --notes-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/release_notes.md" \
            || { echo "::error::could not create v$VERSION at $GITHUB_SHA with the job token; create it with your own (gh release create v$VERSION -R $GITHUB_REPOSITORY --target $GITHUB_SHA --title v$VERSION --generate-notes), then re-run this job"; exit 1; }

      # last so a jsr outage can't cost the tag — and it aborts on a dirty tree, so nothing above it may leave the workspace dirty
      - name: Publish to JSR
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.stage.outputs.zod }}
        working-directory: ./packages/zod
        run: |
          if curl -sf "https://jsr.io/@zod/zod/${VERSION}_meta.json" > /dev/null; then
            echo "@zod/zod@$VERSION is already on JSR"
            exit 0
          fi
          nub exec --node jsr publish --allow-slow-types # --dry-run

      # JSR refuses a version that already exists, so the step checks first; this also lets the first JSR publish of a version already on npm ride on a merge that publishes nothing to npm
      - name: Publish @zod/mini to JSR
        working-directory: ./packages/mini
        run: |
          VERSION=$(nub --node -p 'require("./jsr.json").version')
          if curl -sfL "https://jsr.io/@zod/mini/${VERSION}_meta.json" > /dev/null; then
            echo "@zod/mini@$VERSION is already on JSR"
          else
            nub exec --node jsr publish --allow-slow-types
          fi

      # every zod release from 4.5.0 on must have an @zod/mini twin on npm, whichever of the two stagings above ran
      - run: nub run check:lockstep --wait

# .github/workflows/auto-close.yml
name: Auto-close labeled issues
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * *'     # every day at midnight UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  issues: write
jobs:
  auto-close:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/stale@v11 # Close stale issues & PRs
        with:
          repo-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          stale-issue-label: 'needs-info'     # label you’ll add to trigger closing
          days-before-stale: -1               # don't mark things with needs-info 
          days-before-close: 5              # replace 7 with your X days
          only-labels: 'needs-info'           # ignore all other issues
          remove-stale-when-updated: false
          stale-issue-message: ''
          close-issue-message: ''
files..github/workflows/test.yml:
name: test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - "main"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
      - v4

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test-node:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest]
        node: ["lts/*"]
        typescript: ["5.5", "6", "latest"]
    name: Test with TypeScript ${{ matrix.typescript }} on Node ${{ matrix.node }} (${{ matrix.os }})
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf '%s\n' "${{ matrix.node }}" > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      # Build with the repo-pinned TypeScript: zshy uses the classic compiler API,
      # which TypeScript 7 no longer ships. The matrix version applies to the tests.
      - run: nub run build
      - run: nub add typescript@${{ matrix.typescript }} -Dw
      - run: nub run test
      # test-resolution.ts shells out to zshy, so it can't run under TypeScript 7.
      - run: nub run --filter @zod/resolution test:all
        if: matrix.typescript != 'latest'
      - run: nub run --filter @zod/integration test:all

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        node: ["latest"]
    name: Lint on Node ${{ matrix.node }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf '%s\n' "${{ matrix.node }}" > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: nub run format:check
      - run: nub run lint:check
      - run: nub run check:comments

  check-circular:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    name: Check for circular dependencies
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - run: printf 'latest\n' > .nvmrc
      - uses: nubjs/setup-nub@47e5e7393d50f4e9544ddaf756aa277972afba2d # v0
        with:
          nub-version: "0.8.3"
          node-version: "latest"
      - run: nub install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: nub run check:circular
